NEW DELHI (Reuters) -- Thousands protested in Delhi on Sunday to demand the resignation of India's election chief over a revision of voter lists, the latest in more than a month of opposition demonstrations challenging Prime Minister Narendra Modi.
Led by Rahul Gandhi, a leader of the opposition Congress Party, Sunday's protesters say the revision benefits Modi's Hindu nationalist Bharatiya Janata Party.
The protests and growing support for the opposition form the worst crisis for Modi since he came to power in 2014, though his government remains stable and the next general election is not due until 2029.
Authorities tightened security and warned of traffic diversions before protesters began a march from central Delhi to the designated rally site, where thousands had already assembled.
Hundreds of security personnel, some of them carrying batons and shields and accompanied by riot-control vehicles, surrounded the historic Ramlila Maidan ground as hundreds of people, many waving national and party flags, began moving towards it. Opposition party leaders led the march in an open-top jeep.
Speaking at the rally, Gandhi said Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar would have to vacate his post, and his removal would be the first step towards bringing the country "back on the right track".
The voter roll purge "is the theft of the voice of every single citizen of India. It is the theft of every citizen's right to expression," Gandhi said from the stage."This is an act of betrayal against the nation. This is treason."
Among the protesters listening to him was Reena Mahto, a member of the Congress' student wing, who said four people from her family had been deleted from the voter list due to a false record that they had moved elsewhere.
She told Reuters the family had long lived in Jagdalpur in the central state of Chhattisgarh, but "now all of a sudden we have been marked as shifted from our own house," adding, "There should be accountability, and we are here to seek that."
The change to voter rolls removed over 130 million names - more than the population of Japan. Opposition parties allege the deletions disproportionately affected Muslim voters and members of other minorities who are unlikely to support the BJP.
The Election Commission says the aim of the voter revision is to update voter lists to remove duplicate and ineligible voters. It has denied favouring any party and said wrongly deleted voters can re-enrol.The BJP has accused rivals of trying to undermine democracy by questioning legitimate electoral processes.
Dinesh Singh said he was joining the protest for the sake of his children's future.
"I am not affiliated with any political party," he said. "I am here for a cause. I want the children to remember that we fought for their future."
Health Minister Jagat Prakash Nadda, however, called the protest a "carefully orchestrated drama".
"What is unfolding today at Ramlila Maidan is not an act of respect for democracy. It is a calculated conspiracy to plunge the nation into anarchy, all in the name of democracy," he told news agency ANI.
The demonstration is the latest in a series of near-daily protests that opposition parties, student organisations and the youth-led Cockroach Janta Party have held since late September demanding the resignation of the election chief.
The protests erupted after the Indian Express newspaper reported that Kumar's two deputies had raised several concerns internally about voter list revisions, registration procedures and digital systems.

Nine people dead in Learjet crash in south Florida, officials say

2026-11-02
04:03:23 CET
12:03:23 KST

By Julie Ingwersen
CHICAGO, Nov 1 (Reuters) - A Learjet crashed on Sunday afternoon in a residential area in Palm Beach County, Florida, killing all nine people on board, US transportation officials said.
The private jet had taken off from Austin-Bergstrom International Airport in Texas and was headed to North Eleuthera Airport in the Bahamas, the Federal Aviation Administration said in a statement.
Videos on social media showed the jet slamming into the ground next to a road and exploding.
“It was a big-time tragedy that happened,” Florida Governor Ron DeSantis said at a press conference near the crash site in Lake Worth Beach. “When you see that video, it’s a jarring thing. It was like a missile coming down, and a massive explosion, debris going everywhere.”
The National Transportation Safety Board said it had launched an investigation into the crash, which Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy called a “horrific tragedy.”
FAA records list the Bombardier-made Learjet 60’s owner as a Delaware corporation. Canada-based Bombardier said it would fully support the investigation and cooperate as needed.
The crash left a “massive crater” by the road near the entrance to a mobile home park, Palm Beach County Commissioner Joel Flores said at the news conference. About 600 people were being evacuated from the area and relocated to two shelters in the county, Flores said.
Heavy rainfall and thunderstorms were occurring in the area at the time, forecaster AccuWeather said in a statement.
An audio recording from a Miami air traffic control center posted on LiveATC, a site that broadcasts air traffic control communications, captured the plane’s final moments before the crash in unusual detail.
At first, someone in the plane’s cockpit reported to an air traffic controller that they were “managing the ice” but faced “moderate” turbulence and were seeking “better rides”.
Less than a minute later, the person said “Mayday, mayday,” reporting that the plane was suddenly descending at a rate of 10,000 feet per minute.
Seconds later, the person said they were declaring an emergency, with the rate of descent accelerating to 20,000 feet per minute.
Less than 20 seconds later, the person said: “We’re going to crash into the ground” before saying that the descent rate had reached 22,000 feet per minute as the plane started banking.
About 35 seconds after the initial mayday announcement, the last thing heard from the cockpit was a rapidly spoken “We’re out of time.”
Flight tracking website Flightradar24 said data showed the vertical descent rate at one point exceeded 32,000 feet per minute.
(Reporting by Julie Ingwersen; Editing by Sergio Non, Chizu Nomiyama and Jamie Freed)

SEOUL, Nov 2 (Reuters) - North Korea said on Monday a recent US-South Korean joint military exercise was a nuclear war rehearsal targeting the country and vowed to accelerate efforts to strengthen its nuclear deterrent, according to state media KCNA.
Kim Jong Sik, a deputy department director in the ruling Workers’ Party, said the Iron Mace exercise showed the US remained unchanged in its “wild ambition to stifle North Korea with nukes” and that such threats were “escalating with each passing day.”
He said Iron Mace and other joint military activities by Washington and Seoul underscored the need for North Korea to bolster its nuclear forces at a faster pace.

Yang Moo-jin, a professor emeritus at the University of North Korean Studies, said Kim’s role could be expanding beyond the development and production of missiles to include nuclear and missile policy.
Tensions have escalated between the two Koreas after a border mine explosion in September, with North Korea subsequently threatening to resume loudspeaker propaganda broadcasts toward the South by the end of October.
South Korea’s military said on Monday, however, there were no confirmed indications yet that Pyongyang had followed through on the threat.

Synthesis of the Arts: The Case for Beauty in Architecture and the City
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-11-02
03:00:00 UTC
12:00:00 KST

This article is part of "Thresholds", a special edition printed newspaper by Cobe Notes x ArchDaily.
Post–World War I modernism broke sharply with historicist and neoclassical traditions, stripping buildings of ornamentation and historical or religious reference to focus on priorities, clarity, and efficiency. Architecture embraced rationality and social reform, while art moved in the opposite direction, exploring self-expression, experimentation, and freedom from academic conventions.
This tension between objective order and subjective perception has defined a threshold between the arts evident in contemporary architectural practices, where personal intuition increasingly gives way to measurable facts. Is our pursuit of answers, facts, and truths distancing us from something fundamentally human: questions, doubt, and ambiguity? The answer may lie in public, building-integrated art, a practice that sits precisely at that threshold, and asks practitioners in architecture and urban design to trust values that resist direct measurement.

AI generated
MADRID – Four US citizens and one each from Canada, Japan, Argentina, Mexico, Tunisia and the Czech Republic were among the 69 killed in October’s high-speed train collision in Spain, the authorities said.
The disaster on Oct 28 – one of Europe’s deadliest rail accidents this century – has seen victims’ relatives endure an agonising wait as forensics teams identify the dead, sometimes from individual body parts.
A legal body set up to handle the identification work, made up of police and forensics experts, announced in a statement late on Nov 1 the 10 latest confirmed foreign victims.
It had already announced the deaths of a French and a Portuguese citizen, as well as that of 54 Spaniards.
All but three of the victims are now identified, the statement added.
Three reports for missing people remain active, the authorities said. They concern two Australians and one Japanese citizen.
“As the contacted families have expressed their wish to travel to Spain to carry out in-person identification, we are awaiting their arrival in the country,” the statement said.
The accident was Spain’s second high-speed train collision in 2026 and raised fresh questions about the country’s rail safety, after a crash in the southern region of Andalusia in January killed 46 people.
The latest disaster struck when a service by state operator Renfe ploughed into the back of a stationary train belonging to Spanish company Iryo outside the central village of Urda, around 130km south of Madrid.
The failure of an automatic safety system halted all trains on a 63km stretch of track, but a control centre authorised the Renfe service to resume its journey while the other train was still.
The tragedy came one month before a Nov 29 general election in which Socialist leader Pedro Sanchez will seek to overcome unfavourable polls and extend his eight-year premiership. AFP

Ukraine says Russia used ceasefire to rearm, rotate troops, Kremlin says 'it's normal practice'
Ukraine's General Staff on Monday blasted Russia's actions during a six-day humanitarian ceasefire in Oleshky, saying the Kremlin had used the break in fighting to rearm its forces and rotate troops in the front-line area.

Residents in the Kherson region were warned to be vigilant and told to pay attention to air raid sirens, noting that an intensification of attacks was to be expected after Russia used the brief pause to "strengthen its capabilities."

Ukraine energy provider DTEK on Monday said that emergency power cuts had been initiated in Kyiv and the surrounding region at the request of national grid operator Ukrenergo.

DTEK had previously announced that, "equipment in the region has been seriously damaged due to enemy attacks," adding that energy workers were trying to "restore power to critical infrastructure facilities."
The attacks follow the Kremlin's playbook of seeking to destroy Ukraine's energy infrastructure, especially in cold months, in an attempt to break the will of Ukraine's citizens defending themselves against Russia's invasion by "weaponizing winter."
Ukraine says it evacuated more than 150 from Kherson region before ceasefire expired
Ukraine's military has said that about 170 people were evacuated from the Kherson region (news agencies cite numbers ranging from 167 to 180) before a six-day ceasefire in the Russian-occupied Ukrainian city of Oleshky expired at midnight (Moscow time, 2100 GMT) on Sunday.
No resumption of hostilities was immediately reported after what was the longest pause in fighting since Russian forces invaded in 2022.
Kherson's regional governor on Sunday urged residents remaining behind to avoid "red zones" where he said the threat of Russian strikes "remains high, and the threat to life is extremely high."
Kherson has been subjected to drones attacks, shelling, glide bombs and airdropped mines for nearly five years.
In all, nearly 800 people were reportedly evacuated from the region during the temporary ceasefire, with residents shuttled to Russian-annexed Crimea, then to the Russia town of Anapa, before being flown to Belarus and then Ukraine.
Among those evacuated were 22 children and 21 individuals requiring mobility assistance said Ukraine's army.
US First Lady Melania Trump and Pope Leo XIV — both of whom were reportedly involved in securing the pause in fighting — praised cooperation between the sides, voicing hope that such work might lay the groundwork for a broader peace.
Before Russia launched its illegal invasion on February 24, 2022, and took control of 70% of Kherson, the area was home to more than one million people. Now it is estimated that about 140,000 remain.
Russia hits military facility, cargo vessel, in Ukraine's Odesa
Russia's forces struck a military facility in Ukraine's Odesa region, the Russian Defense Ministry said on Telegram on Monday.
The statement added that a cargo vessel, which the ministry claimed was used for military purposes, was also hit 58 kilometers (36  miles) south of the Black Sea port city of Odesa.
Separately, news agency Reuters cited an official in Odesa as saying that four people had been injured in a Russian attack.
US reportedly pushing to restore Russian gas sales to Europe via Ukraine
The United States is backing a quick resumption of Russian natural gas exports to Europe via pipelines crossing Ukraine as part of talks aimed at securing an energy ceasefire before winter, the Wall Street Journal reported on Sunday, citing US, European and Ukrainian officials.
The proposal involves selling Russian gas via a US intermediary to circumvent European sanctions, the report said, adding that it was mooted by US envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff during trips to Moscow and Kyiv in September.
DW could not immediately verify the report.
Russia's share in European gas supply has declined to about 11% now from 45% on the eve of Moscow's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022.
The European Union currently aims to completely phase out Russian gas imports by the end of 2027. And EU leaders have said they don't want to go back to relying on Russia for energy supplies.
Zelenskyy says Ukraine will stop refinery strikes if US sends Patriot missiles
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said that his country would stop hitting Russian oil refineries if Washington provided Kyiv with powerful Patriot interceptor missiles.
Speaking to US broadcaster Fox News, Zelenskyy said he had had "different and several" conversations with Trump and his team on the issue.
"We asked that we can't not respond after Russia's attack on our energy, after Russia is killing our people, attacks on our electricity, gas, refineries, on everything," he said.
"We said that if you want us not to attack Russia's refineries, they have not to attack our energy system. Another alternative, give us Patriot missiles, we will find money, not just aid," Zelenskyy added.
The Ukrainian leader said if Washington provided the missile systems for one month Kyiv would cease attacks on Russian refineries for the same period.
Asked if he was concerned that this would be seen as trying to "leverage" Trump, Zelenskyy said: "I don't have any concerns when I share the truth between partners."
Ukrainian authorities have been warning for weeks that their supplies of the Patriot interceptor missiles were dwindling.
Ukraine, Russia report separate hacking attacks
Emergency alert apps in both Ukraine and Russia have been hacked, officials said.
Ukraine's air force said an air raid alert app was hacked late on Sunday, with fake alerts being sent to smartphones, warning people of nuclear and chemical threats.
SPRAVDI, Ukraine's Center for Strategic Communications, blamed Russia for the hack in a post on its X account.
Hours later, Moscow said the mobile app of the Russian Emergencies Ministry was hit by "a massive cyberattack."
"Attention! The mobile application of the Ministry of Emergencies of Russia has been subjected to a massive cyberattack, enabling attackers to send false information to the public," the Emergencies Ministry posted on Telegram.
It said authorities were working to fix the issue.
Welcome to our coverage
Hello and welcome to DW's coverage of the latest developments in Russia's war against Ukraine.
As a temporary ceasefire in Russian-occupied Ukrainian town Oleshky ended on Sunday night, Ukraine resumed attacks on Russian oil refineries.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said his country would stop targeting Russian refineries if Washington provided Kyiv with powerful Patriot interceptor missiles to defend against Russian missile and drone strikes.
Meanwhile, Ukraine's air force said it suspected the country's aid raid alert system had been hacked.
Russia's Emergencies Ministry, for its part, said that a "massive cyberattack" hit its application that is designed to warn people of incoming drone attacks and other threats.

Nine people dead in Learjet crash in south Florida, officials say

Unknown Publisher

Nine people dead in Learjet crash in south Florida, officials say
CHICAGO, Nov 1 - A Learjet crashed on Sunday afternoon in a residential area in Palm Beach County, Florida, killing all nine people on board, US transportation officials said.
The private jet had taken off from Austin-Bergstrom International Airport in Texas and was headed to North Eleuthera Airport in the Bahamas, the Federal Aviation Administration said in a statement.
Videos on social media showed the jet slamming into the ground next to a road and exploding.
"It was a big-time tragedy that happened," Florida Governor Ron DeSantis said at a press conference near the crash site in Lake Worth Beach. "When you see that video, it's a jarring thing. It was like a missile coming down, and a massive explosion, debris going everywhere."
The National Transportation Safety Board said it had launched an investigation into the crash, which Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy called a "horrific tragedy."
FAA records list the Bombardier-made Learjet 60's owner as a Delaware corporation. Canada-based Bombardier said it would fully support the investigation and cooperate as needed.
The crash left a "massive crater" by the road near the entrance to a mobile home park, Palm Beach County Commissioner Joel Flores said at the news conference. About 600 people were being evacuated from the area and relocated to two shelters in the county, Flores said.
Heavy rainfall and thunderstorms were occurring in the area at the time, forecaster AccuWeather said in a statement.
An audio recording from a Miami air traffic control center posted on LiveATC, a site that broadcasts air traffic control communications, captured the plane's final moments before the crash in unusual detail.
At first, someone in the plane's cockpit reported to an air traffic controller that they were "managing the ice" but faced "moderate" turbulence and were seeking "better rides".
Less than a minute later, the person said "Mayday, mayday," reporting that the plane was suddenly descending at a rate of 10,000 feet per minute.
Seconds later, the person said they were declaring an emergency, with the rate of descent accelerating to 20,000 feet per minute.
Less than 20 seconds later, the person said: "We're going to crash into the ground" before saying that the descent rate had reached 22,000 feet per minute as the plane started banking.
About 35 seconds after the initial mayday announcement, the last thing heard from the cockpit was a rapidly spoken "We're out of time."
Flight tracking website Flightradar24 said data showed the vertical descent rate at one point exceeded 32,000 feet per minute. REUTERS

Allies fear Trump will target NATO in case of midterm loss
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-11-02
02:35:23 UTC
11:35:23 KST

BRUSSELS — NATO countries are bracing for a worst-case scenario in the U.S. midterm elections Tuesday.
European allies fear a Republican loss could spur President Donald Trump to dramatically step up his attacks on the alliance, according to five NATO diplomats, all of whom were granted anonymity to speak freely on the sensitive issue.
Their worry is that if he is restrained by Congress on domestic policy, Trump, as commander-in-chief of the U.S. military, may seek to cement his legacy on foreign affairs, where he has a freer hand. That could mean pulling thousands more troops out of Europe, three of the diplomats said.
Advertisement
“Usually what happens to lame duck presidents is a mix of venting frustrations and adventurism in foreign policy,” said one senior European defense official. And attacking NATO “seems to be a consistent part of [the] Trump worldview.”
Yet he “remains firm that our NATO allies should have been there for the United States” over the war in Iran, she said, adding: “The President will never settle for the West’s managed decline and will continue to unapologetically advance our interests at home and abroad.”
The worries underscore growing transatlantic tensions after a U.S. cutoff of Starlink satellite services for Ukraine and a fresh rapprochement between Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin weeks before the midterms. Further attacks would deal a fresh blow to NATO, just as Russia steps up its sabotage campaign and so-called hybrid war across Europe.
“He could be very pissed off,” said one of the NATO diplomats. If so, “he’ll be very harsh.”
Advertisement
Forces, money and Ukraine
At the heart of the concerns is an upcoming review of U.S. forces in Europe, expected by December. If Trump is blocked from legislating domestically, he may seek to significantly increase the scope of that pullback to rally his MAGA base, three of the diplomats said.
The president could also decide to tie continued American presence on the continent to Europe accepting a U.S.-backed peace deal in Ukraine, said Oana Lungescu, a former NATO official and distinguished fellow at the Royal United Services Institute think tank.
“There is a risk that all these things — the U.S. force posture review, Ukraine, European security order … somehow are treated as part of a much bigger deal with Putin,” she said, “creating a very dangerous situation for security in Europe.”
Soldiers aboard a helicopter and amphibious vessels take part in a NATO military exercise in Putlos, Germany on Feb. 18, 2026. | Pool photo by Fabian Bimmer via AFP/Getty Images
Trump could also move to cut U.S. contributions to the alliance’s common funding, limit the NATO-backed PURL arms-buying scheme for Ukraine, as well as deepen ties still further with Russia, the diplomats said.
A major electoral defeat for the Republicans could also spell big changes at the Pentagon, which would have knock-on effects for any plans currently being hatched in the building.
Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth has become a deeply unpopular figure in Congress, given his refusal to provide regular briefings about budgets and operations to lawmakers, especially Democrats.
Advertisement
That unpopularity has led to speculation that Hegseth could be out after an electoral blowout for Trump, partially because a Democrat-led Congress would slap Hegseth with probes into his firing of dozens of generals and admirals with no cause, and the faltering war with Iran. Those hearings and investigations would hamstring Hegseth and his team, and could prove embarrassing for the administration.
If Hegseth does move on, there would be a transition period in the Pentagon which could push any decisions about moving U.S. troops out of Europe back by weeks or months.
In theory, a Democrat majority in the House and Senate would restrain Trump’s maneuverability even on foreign and defense issues, even if U.S. law currently imposes a minimum limit of 76,000 on troop presence in Europe.
But “it is doubtful that at least the troop floors would stand up to legal scrutiny and in any case Trump has been very willing to ignore the courts,” said Jennifer Kavanagh, a senior fellow at the Defense Priorities think tank. “The Trump administration has regularly ignored funding guidance from Congress, spending money on activities the legislative branch has not authorized.”
If Trump decides to impose a more sprawling drawdown, Europe will have “the most trouble” replacing assets including electronic warfare capabilities, air defense systems, intelligence and reconnaissance support, aerial refueling, and some types of logistics, she said.
Other allies are more skeptical Trump would hammer NATO. “We have had speculations all the time about Trump ... coming out of the NATO; this has not happened so far,” Montenegrin Defense Minister Dragan Krapović told POLITICO. “Congress is the one making the decision, the final decision about less troops in Europe.”
But “to make assumptions with a high probability of success needs an object of study that makes rational decisions,” said a sixth NATO diplomat. “I don’t think we are there with the current POTUS.”
NATO and the U.S. Department of Defense did not respond to requests for comment by POLITICO.

TAIPEI (Taiwan News) — The Ministry of the Interior said Saturday that three agencies had purchased a total of 32 drones manufactured by Taichung-based Align Corp., after allegations that the company supplied the Army with drones containing Chinese-made chips.
The ministry said in a press release that the National Park Service and Central Police Academy each purchased one Align drone in 2025. The National Immigration Agency awarded a contract to Su Yuan Technology Co. for 30 drones worth NT$2.75 million (US$84,295). The drones have not yet been delivered, but Su Yuan had planned to provide Align-made models.
The ministry said the National Immigration Agency’s contract prohibits delivery of drones manufactured by Align or containing Chinese-made products. It said government drone purchases must comply with non-Chinese supply chain requirements.
The review followed the Army’s discovery of chips marked “CN” during an acceptance inspection in October, per the Liberty Times. The Taichung District Prosecutors Office searched Align’s office and detained Chair Tu Ta-sen (杜大森) and Deputy General Manager Huang Wen-li (黃文麗) after a court approved prosecutors’ request. Prosecutors said two military procurement contracts involving the drones were worth more than NT$8 million.

UN chief condemns death of staff member in Houthi detention in Yemen
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-11-02
02:34:40 UTC
11:34:40 KST

Hazel Belkis Belge
02 November 2026•Update: 02 November 2026
UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres said he was “appalled” by the death of a UN staff member while in the custody of Houthi authorities in Yemen.
Mohammed Ibrahim al-Shami, who worked for the Office of the UN High Commissioner for Human Rights (OHCHR), had been arbitrarily detained by the Houthis since June 6, 2024.
Guterres said in a statement Saturday on the US social media platform X that al-Shami was the second UN employee to die in Houthi detention following the death of a World Food Program (WFP) staff member in February 2025.
“I remain gravely concerned for the safety and well-being of the UN personnel, former UN staff and personnel from humanitarian and civil society organizations who remain detained,” he said in the statement.
The first UN staff member to die in Houthi detention was Ahmed Ba'alawi, a national staff member of the World Food Program, who had been arbitrarily detained by local authorities in northern Yemen since Jan. 23, 2025 and died on Feb. 11 of that year.
Yemen has been mired in conflict since 2014, when Houthi forces seized the capital, Sanaa, prompting a Saudi-led military intervention in March 2015 in support of the internationally recognized government.
The conflict has triggered one of the world's worst humanitarian crises, leaving millions of people dependent on humanitarian assistance.

Former Israeli commander warns Israel faces ‘irreversible collapse’

Unknown Publisher

Zein Khalil and Tarek Chouiref
02 November 2026•Update: 02 November 2026
Retired Israeli Maj. Gen. Itzhak Brik warned Sunday that Israel is facing an irreversible breakdown across its military, economy and institutions, saying it had lost international legitimacy and allies and could not endure prolonged isolation.
In an opinion article published by Israel’s Maariv daily, Brik described the country’s predicament as a comprehensive collapse rather than a political crisis.
He called the results of last Tuesday’s parliamentary elections “the official death certificate of the State of Israel as we knew it,” criticizing television commentators for focusing on seats and coalition negotiations while overlooking deeper problems.
Their coverage, he wrote, resembled an orchestra playing aboard the Titanic in its final moments.
Brik, who formerly commanded military colleges and served as the Ministry of Defense's Ombudsman for Soldiers' Complaints, said Israel had become an international pariah.
“We have lost legitimacy and allies,” he wrote, warning that the country could not remain in complete isolation for long.
He described Israel’s ground forces as suffering a structural collapse and a breakdown in morale, arguing that they lacked the capacity to defend the country against simultaneous threats from within and beyond its borders.
An exhausted army would be unable to stop large-scale incursions or protect civilians in a wider regional war, he warned.
Brik also said that prolonged warfare had driven the national debt to 1.4 trillion shekels ($445 billion). He alleged that economic sanctions, arms restrictions and growing financial isolation were intensifying the pressure.
He dismissed Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s proposal to use cryptocurrencies to counter possible European sanctions as naive and absurd, warning that further deterioration could threaten Israelis’ savings.
Turning to domestic divisions, Brik said Israeli society was experiencing a “silent civil war” rather than polarization alone.
Doctors, scientists, technology entrepreneurs and other skilled professionals were leaving, he said, draining expertise accumulated over decades.
He accused the political leadership of eroding the rule of law and public institutions, with political appointments and unquestioning loyalty taking precedence over competence and integrity.
The Oct. 27 election left Netanyahu’s bloc with 53 seats in the 120-member Knesset compared with 48 for the opposition bloc led by Yashar party leader Gadi Eisenkot and 19 for Arab parties.
Neither main bloc secured the 61 seats needed for a parliamentary majority.

The Arab League called Sunday for an independent international investigation into the torture and systematic abuse of Palestinians from Gaza held in Israel’s Ramla Prison, demanding accountability for those responsible.
In a statement, the league condemned the repeated assaults of prisoners in the facility’s Rakevet wing, saying they had left detainees with injuries and burns.
It described the practices as violations of international humanitarian law, including the Geneva Conventions and the Convention against Torture, and said they constituted “crimes against humanity” requiring accountability.
The league demanded an immediate end to the abuse and urged Israel to allow unrestricted access for the International Committee of the Red Cross and independent monitors to document conditions and provide medical care.
It also called for the immediate release of sick and wounded prisoners and an end to arbitrary detention.
The statement followed an Oct. 27 report by the Palestinian Prisoners’ Media Office detailing recurring assaults against Gaza detainees in the Rakevet wing.
The office said the assaults took place on Fridays and Saturdays and involved beatings with batons, pepper spray, gas, rubber bullets and stun grenades.
It also reported that guards entered a cell with police dogs and took detainees to a room without surveillance cameras, where they were assaulted.
The office warned that continued abuse endangered prisoners’ lives, particularly those already ill or injured.
The Arab League urged the international community, the UN Human Rights Council and the UN General Assembly to act to protect Palestinian prisoners and end impunity.
There was no immediate Israeli response to the statement.
Ramla Prison is in central Israel and is administered by the Israel Prison Service.

Algeria launches new cleanup of former French nuclear test site
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-11-02
02:05:36 UTC
11:05:36 KST

Hassen Djebril and Tarek Chouiref
02 November 2026•Update: 02 November 2026
Algeria launched a second operation Sunday to remove radioactive waste from a former French nuclear test site in the Sahara Desert, its Defense Ministry said, accusing Paris of withholding information needed for the cleanup.
The operation is taking place at the "Beryl E2" test tunnel site in the In Ekker area of the southern province of Tamanrasset.
Algerian teams are carrying out the work under Defense Ministry supervision in coordination with the national agency responsible for rehabilitating former French nuclear test sites, according to a ministry statement.
The cleanup involves identifying radioactive areas, collecting nuclear waste and storing it in specially designated concrete containers. The ministry said the work would follow national and international safety standards.
It accused France of evading its responsibilities and refusing to provide records and maps showing where nuclear waste was buried.
The ministry said the remaining contamination continued to hinder development in In Ekker and Reggane, in the southwestern province of Adrar.
Algeria began its first partial cleanup operation on Feb. 14 at Taourirt Tan Affella in the In Ekker area, according to the Algerian Press Service.
France conducted its first nuclear test near Reggane in the Sahara Desert on Feb. 13, 1960 while Algeria was under French colonial rule. The test was code-named Gerboise Bleue, or Blue Jerboa.
France carried out 17 nuclear tests in the Algerian Sahara between 1960 and 1966, continuing the program for four years after Algeria gained independence in 1962.
Algeria has long sought access to records and maps of the tests and waste burial sites to identify contaminated areas and address their consequences.
The legacy of French colonial rule remains a source of disputes between the two countries.

Netanyahu does not rule out PM rotation with Eisenkot, despite Likud's public stance
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-11-02
02:04:21 UTC
11:04:21 KST

Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has not ruled out the possibility of a rotation agreement for the premiership as part of forming a unity government. Asked in closed-door discussions about the possibility of establishing a unity government with a rotating prime minister, Netanyahu replied: "We are examining everything. I am not completely ruling out any option."
Sources close to the prime minister who discussed the issue with him came away with the impression that he had left the matter open and was indeed considering every possible option. One of his associates said Sunday in response: "No proposal to form a unity government has been made yet."
In contrast to Netanyahu's remarks behind closed doors, Likud ministers and lawmakers who have addressed the unity government issue in recent days have given the impression that there would be no rotation agreement, since Netanyahu would not agree to serve as prime minister for only part of a term. Coalition Chairman Ofir Katz even issued an ultimatum Sunday, saying that if the change bloc ousts Knesset Speaker Amir Ohana, a unity government would not be possible.
Netanyahu himself, however, has not closed the door to a rotation agreement with Gadi Eisenkot, chairman of the Yashar! party. Netanyahu, who has yet to comment publicly on the possibility of forming a unity government or agreeing to a rotation, is deeply concerned about the change bloc forming a government with ultra-Orthodox and Arab parties, either as coalition partners or with their support from outside. He believes such a government could survive for a long time, potentially keeping him out of the prime minister's office altogether. "Our fear is that a government with Arabs and ultra-Orthodox parties, even with Shas' six seats, could last an entire term," a senior Likud official said.
On Sunday, amid those concerns, Netanyahu continued his campaign against the Arab parties and also addressed the ultra-Orthodox issue. "Eisenkot and his partners are trampling on the trust of Israel's citizens. They are breaking all their promises regarding cooperation with parties that support terrorism and are working to form a government with them. And in the ultimate display of contempt, after four years of relentless attacks on the ultra-Orthodox community, they are abandoning ultra-Orthodox conscription out of a lust for power. This must not be allowed to happen," Likud said in a statement.
Eisenkot's plan
For now, the change bloc is not pursuing a unity government. Instead, it is working on two parallel tracks: gaining control of key positions of power in the Knesset and forming a narrow government. According to political assessments, a narrow government led by Eisenkot could be established with outside support from Ra'am and United Torah Judaism as a coalition partner.
Meanwhile, the possibility of cooperating with Eisenkot is causing disagreements within United Torah Judaism. While Yitzhak Goldknopf is interested in advancing support for Eisenkot, Meir Porush expressed skepticism about the move Sunday, saying: "Eisenkot? Who would go with him? He hasn't even called us."
Within United Torah Judaism, party officials understand that even without actively supporting Eisenkot, they can influence the first parliamentary moves of the 26th Knesset and potentially use that leverage to pressure Netanyahu. Senior party members are discussing the possibility of abstaining in a vote to replace Knesset Speaker Amir Ohana, a move that could allow the opposition to oust him without requiring United Torah Judaism to vote actively in favor.
At a meeting Sunday evening attended by senior party figures Yaakov Asher, Yitzhak Goldknopf and Meir Porush, it was decided that the issue would be discussed only after receiving a concrete proposal from Eisenkot. According to party sources, United Torah Judaism also decided that, at this stage, it would not recommend any candidate for prime minister.
Eisenkot is working to assemble a list of parties that will recommend him during consultations at the President's Residence, which are scheduled to begin Wednesday. Senior figures in the change bloc said it was important for the Yashar! chairman to be the first to receive the mandate to form a government.
A senior figure who is not a member of Eisenkot's party warned Sunday: "If the entire bloc does not recommend Eisenkot, all the judicial overhaul laws passed by the current coalition will take effect on January 1, 2027, as stipulated by law."
The legislation includes the law concerning the attorney general, the Police Internal Investigations Department law and the law changing the composition of the Judicial Selection Committee. Under the change bloc's plan, if President Isaac Herzog gives Eisenkot the mandate to form a government before Netanyahu, Eisenkot would also gain control of the Knesset's Arrangements Committee. That committee could decide two major issues on the change bloc's agenda: replacing the Knesset speaker and repealing the judicial overhaul laws.
Former Prime Minister Naftali Bennett's B'Yachad party announced Sunday that it would recommend Eisenkot to the president as its candidate to form the government. The change bloc also expects the Democrats to recommend Eisenkot.
The one leader who has yet to express a position on the matter, even in closed-door discussions among the change bloc's leaders, is Yisrael Beytenu Chairman Avigdor Liberman.
- Shilo Freid contributed to this report.

2026-11-02

Tarek Chouiref
02 November 2026•Update: 02 November 2026
Yemen’s army said Sunday that its forces had “neutralized” nearly 500 Houthi fighters and field commanders during 1,272 operations over the previous 24 hours.
Army spokesman Majed al-Nuzaili said the operations destroyed or damaged 169 vehicles, pieces of equipment and heavy weapons. His statement did not specify how many of those described as neutralized were killed or wounded.
In a statement on the US social media platform X, al-Nuzaili said the attacks targeted Houthi positions, reinforcements, fortifications, firing positions and supply routes as part of Operation Dawn of Yemen.
He said the operations supported ground advances and the recapture of positions on the Al-Jawf front in northern Yemen.
Government forces were also continuing operations in Marib, Al-Bayda, Lahj and Taiz provinces, according to the spokesman.
In Taiz, al-Nuzaili said army troops and allied Popular Resistance fighters were battling the Houthis with support from warplanes, drones and artillery.
He said forces were taking precautions to protect civilians and civilian infrastructure.
Earlier, the army announced that it had downed two Houthi drones and carried out airstrikes on the group’s positions in Al-Misrakh district, south of Taiz.
The Interior Ministry separately said a Houthi drone strike on a home in western Taiz killed a woman and a girl and wounded another woman.
In al-Jawf, government forces said Saturday that they had secured the strategic Huwayshian mountain range, which they described as a forward defensive line for the Houthi-held provincial capital, al-Hazm.
Since Oct. 5, Yemeni government forces have launched Operation Dawn of Yemen to restore state institutions from Houthi control and retake the capital, Sanaa.
A military escalation between government forces and the Houthis resumed in July, killing and wounding thousands and displacing more than a quarter of a million people, according to UN reports.
The escalation ended a period of relative calm that had prevailed in Yemen since April 2022, while the humanitarian crisis has worsened amid continued fighting and displacement.
Yemen has been at war since the Houthis seized Sanaa and several provinces in September 2014, prompting a Saudi-led coalition to intervene in March 2015 in support of the internationally recognized government.

The IDF’s winter recruitment cycle for young haredi (ultra-Orthodox) men entering combat support roles began Sunday morning, as behind-the-scenes coalition negotiations with the haredi parties continued amid disagreements over the conscription bill.
Several dozen prospective recruits arrived at the Meitav recruitment center at Tel Hashomer during the first stage of the process. Military officials reported no unusual incidents, described the enlistment as a positive trend, and expressed cautious optimism about meeting recruitment targets.
To prepare for expanded haredi enlistment, Brig. Gen. Amir Vadmani, head of the Personnel Directorate’s manpower staff, led extensive planning to refine recruitment tracks and service conditions tailored to haredi recruits. Military officials in the Technology and Logistics Directorate told Walla that changes made over the past year were intended to accommodate more haredi recruits across its various service tracks, including combat support roles.
Haredi recruitment numbers rise
According to Personnel Directorate figures, more than 1,200 haredim enlisted in 2023, approximately 2,800 in 2024, and approximately 4,300 in 2025, an increase of about 53% from the previous year.
For the 2026 recruitment year, which runs from July 2026 to July 2027, the IDF has set a target of approximately 4,800 haredi recruits. It aims to recruit a record number into combat and combat support roles, expanding enlistment beyond maintenance, software, and administrative positions.

Mallory McMorrow, who also ran in the Democratic primary against El-Sayed; and pro-Palestinian politicians including Michigan state Senate candidate Abbas Alawieh, a co-founder of the “Uncommitted” movement in 2024 that targeted then-President Joe Biden at the ballot box over Gaza.
Their joint message: All Democrats, Jewish and not, should back El-Sayed and reject Stevens’ endorsement of Rogers.
Democrat Scholten voices disapproval of El-Sayed
Simultaneously, another Democrat, Michigan Rep. Hillary Scholten, appeared with several rabbis to address a different audience of Jews uncomfortable with El-Sayed’s rhetoric on Israel.
On that Zoom following Scholten’s appearance, some leaders of the Nonnegotiable movement urged their group of Jewish voters to write in “Emma Lazarus,” the 19th-century Jewish poet and activist whose words grace the base of the Statue of Liberty, on their ballots instead.
Scholten did not urge the Jews on the call in one direction or another, nor did she mention Stevens. But she has publicly voiced her own disapproval of El-Sayed and refused to endorse him.
“We know that in this moment, it has never, ever been more important to stand up and push back against antisemitism that has been given far, far too much of a platform in American politics,” she told the Zoom crowd.
One of Nonnegotiable’s organizers, Rabbi Aaron Starr of Congregation Shaarey Zedek in the Detroit suburb of Southfield, told people on the call that he has “profound respect for Haley Stevens.”
“I have profound respect for her willingness to put herself out there,” Starr said. “I have deep respect for her willingness to stand up, to speak out and take a stand in this difficult moment.”
The dual perspectives epitomized the dilemma many of Michigan’s Jewish voters are facing in the campaign’s final days. A sizable contingent of the state’s Jews are increasingly troubled by El-Sayed’s statements on Israel and antisemitic acts, including his recent refusal to name whether Israel or Iran posed a greater threat to the United States.
Some, including Stevens’ fiancée Jason Turkish, a Democratic megadonor, have publicly said they would vote for Rogers.
Jewish voices condemn Stevens'
Yet the race, which is one of several pivotal to Democrats taking control of the Senate, has also troubled many liberal Jews who see GOP policies as deeply antithetical to their beliefs. Many for that reason view Stevens’ endorsement, which she said was meant to stand “against hate,” as a betrayal.
New York Jewish progressive congressional candidate Brad Lander castigated Stevens in a video from Brooklyn.
“Maybe she doesn’t care about throwing away reproductive rights, throwing away civil rights,” said Lander, who has spoken to Michigan Jews in support of El-Sayed. “But to do it all in the name of so-called Jewish safety, boy, as an American Jew I can tell you that’s not the way that anybody, Jews or Muslims or anybody else, will be saved.”
Ray Wert, McMorrow’s Jewish husband, said on X that he had urged Stevens to sign her name to an op-ed condemning Rogers for his own interactions with antisemitic individuals, including a major donor who promotes Christian nationalism and a former student campaign organizer who had tweeted about wanting to send Jews to North Korea. She refused, Wert claimed.
He posted a copy of the op-ed, which included the line, “I can’t hold one standard for Democrats and a softer one for Republicans and still claim to have a standard at all.”

Railway minister Ashwini Vaishnaw witnessed the test at BEML’s Bengaluru facility on Sunday.
NEW DELHI: Paving the way for final production of the country’s first indigenous Bullet Train, B28, the “Squeeze Test” or vehicle body shell test of the first coach is underway and will be completed next week. Railway minister Ashwini Vaishnaw witnessed the test at BEML’s Bengaluru facility on Sunday.A squeeze test is a safety assessment to determine whether a train’s car body can withstand heavy external forces and pressure without excessive deformation or structural failure in case of a collision or crash. “Squeeze test of the integrated car body is at final stage. After this, propulsion system will be placed and all electronic systems will be put in place. Subsequently, a climatic test will be carried out wherein the car will be subjected to tests at high temperature of 50 degree Celsius and negative temperature, and dusty and heavy rain environment conditions,” Vaishnaw said.
Railways plans to start the test run of the high-speed train, designed to operate at a maximum speed of 249 kmph and a testing speed of 275 kmph, from first quarter of 2027-2028 on Surat-Vapi (100 km) section of Ahmedabad-Mumbai High Speed corridor.
The commercial run is scheduled for August 2027. Each bullet train will have eight coaches and another eight can be added later. The eight-car train can carry 557 passengers.BEML, a central PSU, is manufacturing the first two of the indigenous bullet trains, each comprising eight coaches.
“After the successful completion of this test, the prototype should ideally be ready in less than six months. Since the B28 (Bharat 28) train is not being built on Japanese Shinkansen technology, the development process should not take much time. The squeeze test establishes whether the body retains its shape under pressure and whether the passenger compartment maintains its structural integrity,” an official said.While seeking Cabinet approval for the escalated cost of the country’s first bullet train project, the railway ministry had stated that two prototype trains were expected to be ready for trial runs in the first quarter of 2027. It had also said that the entire Gujarat section of the corridor was expected to be completed by December 2027, while the full 508-km Mumbai-Ahmedabad High Speed Rail corridor is targeted for completion by December 2030.

What is celebrated on November 2 in Ukraine and around the world
Ukraine
Unknown Publisher
2026-11-02
03:45:29 EET
10:45:29 KST

What is celebrated on November 2 in Ukraine and around the world
Kyiv • UNN
November 2 marks the international days for the protection of journalists, vitiligo awareness, and stress awareness. Believers honor the martyrs.
On November 2, under the auspices of the UN, the world observes the International Day to End Impunity for Crimes against Journalists; at the call of the WHO and medical organizations, World Vitiligo Day and Stress Awareness Day are also held. According to the church calendar under the new style, Saint Martyr Akindynos, Saint Martyr Pegasius and the 7,000 martyrs with them are commemorated, while under the old style, Saint Great Martyr Artemius of Antioch is remembered, UNN reports.
International Day to End Impunity for Crimes against Journalists
An official international UN date proclaimed by the General Assembly in 2013. The date was chosen to commemorate two French journalists — Claude Verlon and Ghislaine Dupont — who were killed while carrying out their professional duties in Mali on November 2, 2013. The event calls on governments to investigate cases of violence, threats, abductions and killings of media workers, bring those responsible to justice, and create safe conditions for journalists to fulfill their civic duty.
World Vitiligo Day
The date aims to promote awareness of vitiligo — a chronic autoimmune skin disease characterized by loss of pigmentation and the appearance of white patches on the body. The event is intended to dispel myths about the contagiousness of the disease, combat the stigmatization of patients in society, provide psychological support to those affected, and raise funds for research into dermatological disorders.
International Stress Awareness Day
Established in 1998 on the initiative of the International Stress Management Association. The event focuses on highlighting the impact of prolonged psycho-emotional stress on people's physical health, preventing professional burnout, developing emotional self-regulation skills, and promoting accessible methods of psychological self-help.
All Souls' Day
A commemorative day in the Western Christian calendar that follows All Saints' Day. Established by Saint Odilo of Cluny in the 10th century, the observance is dedicated to prayers for the souls of deceased Christians who are in Purgatory. In many countries around the world, people visit cemeteries, light candles on the graves of relatives, and order requiem Masses.
Under the new calendar, Orthodox and Greek Catholic believers commemorate the holy martyrs Akindynos, Pegasius, Aphthonius, Elpidiphorus, Anemodistus and the 7,000 martyrs with them. They were prominent Christians at the court of the Persian King Shapur II. Openly professing their faith before the ruler, they endured brutal tortures, during which they displayed steadfastness and worked miracles through prayer. The miraculous healing of the martyrs and their steadfastness converted thousands of Persians to Christ, and they accepted martyrdom together with them.
Under the old calendar, believers commemorate Saint Great Martyr Artemius of Antioch — a distinguished military commander and governor of Egypt who exposed Emperor Julian the Apostate's persecution of Christians and suffered martyrdom by beheading in 362.

RLWC quick hits: Chase for glory wide open heading into semifinals
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-11-02
01:42:39 UTC
10:42:39 KST

Fri, 11 Sept, 7:50 pm, Final score, Rabbitohs 10, Knights 20
Rugby League World Cup quick hits: Australia's grip on favouritism slips, Kiwi duo close in on history
The group stage of the Rugby League World Cup is in the books after a remarkable double-header to finish things off.
Lebanon's golden-point win over France and Tonga and Samoa's epic showdown were both classics, giving the tournament the close finishes that have been in short supply.
With Australia, New Zealand, Tonga and Samoa progressing to the semifinals, here are the quick hits from the final round of matches.
1. Was this the last World Cup for the old Kumuls?
No country in rugby league will see the sport transform in their nation from this World Cup to the next like Papua New Guinea.
The entry of the PNG Chiefs to the NRL in 2028, with their near-limitless resources and game-bending salary cap concessions, will change the game in the land where they love it most.
So long as the Chiefs fulfil their promise of creating strong pathways for local talent to make it to the top level, it has the potential to change the national side forever.
The prospect of talents like five-eighth Gairo Voro, who scored a sharp solo try, or winger Dudley Dutoi, who got the better of England star Dom Young, getting regular NRL football is a tantalising one.
The two were among Papua New Guinea's best in a spirited defeat, and from the Highlands to the islands of New Britain there can be so many more like them.
PNG's improvement over the past decade has been steady, but it is about to hit overdrive. This game against England might be the last dance for the Kumuls as we've come to know them.
2. The New Zealand duo closing in on history
It was another Kiwi romp as New Zealand punished a Fiji side that struggled to backup from last week's fine performance against Australia, but amid the near-endless tries and ill-tempered flare-ups, Casey McLean and Jamayne Isaako continued their march towards history.
Isaako scored 26 points from a try and 13 goals from as many attempts to go with his 38 points against the Cook Islands the weeks before, and the winger is closing in on Shaun Johnson's all-time Kiwi pointscoring record.
The former Dolphin has 215 points from his 17 Tests, just 10 shy of Johnson's mark, and could claim top spot as early as the World Cup final if the points continue to flow for Stacey Jones's side.
McLean has more work to do to run down Manu Vatuvei as the nation's highest-ever try-scorer, but he is making a cracking pace.
In just seven Tests, McLean has scored 15 tries to sit in equal-eighth spot on the all-time list. Every other player around him had at least 20 caps, and Vatuvei took 29 to collect his 23 tries.
The second four-try haul of his budding career means that at just 20, McLean is odds on to become New Zealand's Test try-scoring king sooner rather than later.
3. Are Australia still the favourites?
The Kangaroos are one of only two unbeaten sides heading into the knockout phase, but their hold on favouritism is shaky at best.
Their brilliant win over New Zealand in the tournament opener had more than a few elements of fortune in their favour, especially the two length-of-the-field intercept tries that kept them in the game early on.
They scratched their way past Fiji and romped home against the Cook Islands since, looking short of their best in both performances.
While they are always a threat, it feels as though all four nations in the semifinals are in with a chance of lifting the trophy rather than it being Australia's birthright.
Kevin Walters has a big decision to make at halfback between Tom Dearden and Sam Walker but seems to have settled on Reece Walsh as his custodian, and after the Broncos playmaker laid on five tries in this 66-6 mauling to go with his game-changing plays against the Kiwis, it's hard to argue.
4. Lebanon-France is what the World Cup can be
After a tournament filled with blowouts, the epic finish between France and Lebanon shows what's possible when things line up right at the World Cup, as two winless teams desperate to restore some pride played out a classic.
This was two teams of similar skill levels in front of a rowdy and emotionally invested crowd at a venue that accentuated at least one of the fan bases.
That's a simple recipe to follow, and while you won't always be rewarded with the epic finish of this golden point thriller, a new format that keeps teams like this together and therefore produces more of these match-ups is a must for 2030.
When that next tournament rolls around, plenty of tales from this game will be told, from Cesar Rouge's game-winning field goal controversially chalked off the board to Lebanon's remarkable extra-time try to Abbas Miski.
That score put the tragedy of French fullback Arthur Mourgue, a mad genius who doesn't always nail the genius part, into World Cup folklore after his remarkable field goal sent the game to extra time before a maniac kick inside his own 20 fell for the Cedars's winning try.
5. The veteran Tonga cannot do without
Amid a match with a galaxy of stars that promised a glorious future for Samoa and Tonga, Tui Lolohea seemed the odd man out.
The Tongan veteran was the only player in the game who doesn't ply his trade in the NRL, and given his mercurial career, he might have seemed a weak link for the Mate Ma'a.
But after 12 seasons in the red jersey, Lolohea has proven himself an invaluable part of their rise to the top of Test football, and while they have more talent at their disposal than ever before, they always come back to him when it counts.
Along with Jason Taumalolo, Lolohea is the only man to have played in each of Tonga's most important wins over the past decade and always seems to defy critics when it matters most.
He is older and slower, but he always gives Tonga what they need — the 31-year-old, who currently doesn't have a club for next season, set up a try for Jojo Fifita with a clever floating pass and held up well in defence under heavy pressure from Samoa, who clearly targeted the former Huddersfield Giant.
With Latu Fainu fit and Talatau Amone in the squad, Tonga are not short of options in the halves, but Lolohea rewarded coach Kristian Woolf's faith yet again, as he always seems to do when it matters most.

Ukrainian Film Festival kicks off in Poland on Nov 2, with 50 films to be screened in 12 cities
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-11-02
01:40:00 UTC
10:40:00 KST

Ukrainian Film Festival kicks off in Poland on Nov 2, with 50 films to be screened in 12 cities
Beata Bieronska-Lach, director of the Ukraine! Film Festival, announced this in an interview with Ukrinform.
According to her, despite the full-scale war, Ukraine's film industry continues to develop, particularly thanks to international cooperation and foreign funding.
"Every year, I worry about whether we will have enough Ukrainian films and whether there will be anything to screen. I fear that film production might grind to a halt under wartime conditions... However, my concerns have proved unfounded: Ukrainian films are being made. If not directly in Ukraine, then through numerous international co-productions. Ukrainian filmmakers have started looking for funding abroad, and they are succeeding. There are many funds that finance Ukrainian cinema," Bieronska-Lach said.
She said that this year's festival program will include Polish-Ukrainian and German-Ukrainian co-productions. The competition program will feature eight full-length fiction films, nine documentaries and 23 short films. Screenings of children's films and a separate section dedicated to Belarusian cinema are also planned.
The festival director noted that after the screenings in Warsaw, the festival will continue in 11 other cities: Krakow, Wroclaw, Gdansk, Lublin, Gliwice, Lodz, Rzeszow, Plock, Bielsko-Biala, Zielona Gora and Poznan. The screenings will run until mid-December.
The organizer said the festival's geographical reach is changing. This year, screenings will not take place in Torun because the institution that previously hosted the event is undergoing restructuring. At the same time, new cities and organizations are joining the festival.
"Overall, the cities and cinemas that hosted the festival in previous years want to continue working with us. At the same time, new institutions are emerging and approaching us on their own initiative because they want to screen Ukrainian films," Bieronnska-Lach said.
According to her, these are most often Polish organizations, foundations or cinemas seeking to respond to demand from local communities. In cities with large Ukrainian communities, such screenings make it possible to organize joint cultural events for Ukrainians and Poles and promote integration within local communities.
The festival director said that Bielsko-Biala and Zielona Gora are the new venues this year. According to her, the cities themselves expressed interest in joining the event.
Bieronnska-Lach also noted that Polish cinemas continue to show interest in Ukrainian films. Last year, she feared that amid some cooling in Ukrainian-Polish relations, cinemas would gradually lose interest and withdraw from screenings, sometimes suggesting postponing them until the following year.
"Instead, we can see today that interest remains, which means the films will be screened in various cities," Bieronnska-Lach said.

Federal Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt also accused “violent left-wing groups and troublemakers from migrant communities” of hijacking initially peaceful demonstrations, according to Bild.
“The rioters and looters will be identified and held accountable,” he said.
Immigration and crime have long been contentious issues in Germany, where people have more recently become dissatisfied with the rising cost of living and German Chancellor Friedrich Merz. Fatigue with Berlin’s immigration policy has driven the success of Alternative for Germany (AfD), the second-largest party in the Bundestag, which finished first in state elections in Saxony-Anhalt and Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania in September, marking its first victories in those two states.
An October poll by Forsa found that 87% of Germans were dissatisfied with Merz’s performance, while just 11% were satisfied. The survey also showed that 61% of supporters of his own CDU/CSU alliance were unhappy with his leadership.
The riots in Frankfurt coincided with a broader wave of protests across Europe over rising living costs, housing shortages, and deteriorating public services. In France, demonstrators clashed with police in Paris during protests against government policies, while Spain and Italy have also seen demonstrations over housing costs, wages, and economic pressure.

Li said he entered the competition with the mindset of challenging his opponents. "I'll take it one match at a time and fight for every point. I can't afford to relax on any point," he said.
The Dakar YOG marks the first time an Olympic sporting event has been held on African soil. Competitions are being staged across Dakar, Diamniadio and Saly, combining sport with cultural exchange as the Olympic movement opens a new chapter on the continent.
Nine gold medals will be up for grabs on Monday in swimming, judo, coastal rowing beach sprints and rugby sevens. ■

Antonelli becomes youngest F1 champion as Verstappen wins Mexico City GP
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-11-02
09:36:29 CST
10:36:29 KST

Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli (top) of Italy celebrates being crowned the Formula One World Champion with Red Bull Racing's Max Verstappen (L) of the Netherlandsand and Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton of Britain at the Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez in Mexico City, Mexico, Nov. 1, 2026. (Photo by Francisco Canedo/Xinhua)
by F1 correspondent Michael Butterworth
BEIJING, Nov. 2 (Xinhua) -- Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli became the youngest world champion in Formula 1 history on Sunday after finishing third in the Mexico City Grand Prix, ending Italy's 73-year wait for a drivers' title.
The 20-year-old secured his maiden championship with four races to spare, eclipsing Sebastian Vettel's previous record by more than three years and becoming the first Italian to win the title since Alberto Ascari claimed his second consecutive crown in 1953.
Red Bull's Max Verstappen won a chaotic race at the Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez, holding off Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton by 0.799 seconds, but the afternoon belonged to Antonelli, whose composed drive completed a remarkable transformation from an inconsistent rookie into Formula 1's newest champion.
At 20 years and 68 days old, Antonelli broke the record set by Vettel, who was 23 years and 134 days old when he won his first championship with Red Bull in 2010.
It also marked a striking reversal of fortunes within Mercedes. In his debut season in 2025, Antonelli had been comprehensively outscored and outperformed by teammate George Russell, raising questions over whether his promotion to F1 had come too soon.
Twelve months later, the Italian has emphatically answered those doubts, establishing himself as Mercedes' leading driver and leaving his more experienced British teammate firmly in the shade.
Antonelli claimed his maiden Grand Prix victory in China, the second round of the season, before embarking on a remarkable run of success that established him as the championship favorite.
His ninth victory of the season at last weekend's United States Grand Prix left him on the brink of the championship, with only Russell and Hamilton retaining mathematical hopes of denying him the title.
Starting fourth in Mexico City, Antonelli needed only to finish ninth to secure the crown. He remained largely clear of the incidents that disrupted the race before overtaking Ferrari's Charles Leclerc following a red-flag restart to move into third place.
The Italian maintained that position to the chequered flag, becoming visibly emotional as his race engineer Peter Bonnington congratulated him over the team radio.
"We did it! Thank you so much," Antonelli said, struggling to contain his emotions.
"I wouldn't be here without Mercedes, without my family, so I'm very grateful for this moment and it's one that will live forever," he added after the race.
While Antonelli celebrated, Verstappen claimed his third victory in four races after capitalizing on a fierce opening-lap battle between Ferrari teammates Hamilton and Leclerc.
Hamilton had started from pole position but lost the lead amid a frantic opening sequence, with Verstappen emerging ahead as the Ferrari drivers fought for position.
The race was interrupted by a lengthy red flag following a heavy crash for Cadillac's Valtteri Bottas, whose car suffered a suspension failure, before further incidents and safety car periods disrupted the closing stages.
At the restart, Verstappen and Hamilton made contact while battling for the lead, but the Dutchman retained his advantage and held off the seven-time world champion to take victory.
Despite struggling badly with flat-spotted tyres, Leclerc just held off McLaren's Lando Norris to take fourth, while Russell endured a frustrating afternoon to finish sixth, further underlining the contrasting fortunes of the Mercedes teammates.
Oscar Piastri took seventh for McLaren, followed by Alpine's Franco Colapinto, Racing Bulls' Liam Lawson and Colapinto's teammate Pierre Gasly.
Antonelli now holds an unassailable 119-point championship lead, while Verstappen has moved into second place in the standings. Russell has slipped to fourth, 130 points behind his teammate.
Mercedes also remains on course for the constructors' championship, holding a 126-point advantage over Ferrari ahead of next weekend's Sao Paulo Grand Prix. ■

Kyrgyzstan’s industrial output rises 7% to $7.83B in 9M2026
Kyrgyzstan’s industrial output from January through September 2026 totaled 685.4 billion soms ($7.83 billion), up 7% in physical terms from a year earlier, the National Statistical Committee said, Trend reported.
Growth came from higher output in several manufacturing industries and in mining.
Chemical production rose 2.3 times and refined oil products 1.9 times. Wood and paper products and printing grew 41.3%, motor vehicles 39.4%, construction materials 29.1% and pharmaceuticals 13.6%.
Food, beverages and tobacco rose 9.4% and mining 7.3%. The committee also reported growth in electricity, gas and steam supply, linked to higher distribution of electricity and gas.
Industry grew much more slowly than construction, where output rose 1.6 times to 380 billion soms. Agricultural output rose 6.5% to 399.5 billion soms ($4.57 billion).

Tens of thousands build 108 Buddhist stupas for Bhutan ‘mindfulness’ city

Unknown Publisher

Tens of thousands build 108 Buddhist stupas for Bhutan ‘mindfulness’ city
Bhutan is creating a ‘mindfulness’ city aimed at driving economic growth and persuading more young people to stay.
Tens of thousands of volunteers have taken part in building 108 Buddhist stupas in Bhutan’s new “mindfulness” city, as the Himalayan kingdom embarks on an ambitious project to boost economic growth.
The 15-metre-tall (50ft) stupas, sacred Buddhist monuments found across the Himalayas, were installed on Sunday along 12km (7.5 miles) of riverbank near the Indian border, at the site of the future Gelephu Mindfulness City.
More than 40,000 volunteers participated in building the structures as “a physical form of prayer made permanent in stone and earth”, after starting work after midnight, officials said. The number 108 is sacred in Buddhism, widely practised in Bhutan.
About 200,000 people attended the ceremony, or nearly a fourth of the population, officials told the AFP news agency.
“I was worried that raising 108 stupas in a single day might not succeed,” Bhutan’s King Jigme Khesar Namgyel Wangchuck said in a speech at the ceremony.
“But everything went successfully, and for that, I am truly grateful.”
Bhutanese leaders hope that Gelephu Mindfulness City, conceived by the king and designed by Danish architects, will boost the country’s economy and persuade more young people to stay, attracting investment in sustainable business, green technology, education, tourism and financial services.
Bhutan is facing massive economic challenges, from rising unemployment and falling birth rates to the mass migration of skilled workers.
The city, currently a small town with a population of about 10,000, is in southern Bhutan, along the border with India, about 240km (150 miles) south of Thimphu, the nation’s capital.
The king established the special zone by royal charter in 2024, saying its purpose was to “create a vibrant economic hub”.
The landlocked Himalayan nation, with a population of just under 800,000 and wedged between China and India, is known for its policy of prioritising “Gross National Happiness” alongside economic growth.
“This occasion will be recorded in our history for generations to come,” said Nima Gyeltshen, 65, head of the Organisation for Youth Empowerment, which helps young Bhutanese find work.
Cryptocurrency ambitions
Analysts have questioned whether Bhutan can attract sufficient investment to realise its vision for the new city.
But Indian billionaire Gautam Adani, head of the ports-to-power conglomerate, joined the project as a founding member in January.
The site is set to be connected to India’s rail network in neighbouring Assam, with an international airport slated to open in 2029.
The project is also linked to Bhutan’s cryptocurrency ambitions, with the kingdom mining Bitcoin using surplus hydropower and pledging to use digital assets to support the city’s development.
Bishnu Maya Moktang, a resident who attended Sunday’s ceremony, said she was excited about the upcoming mindfulness city.
“I hope to live long enough to see it,” Moktang, 56, told AFP.
“My parents died young, and they would never see the city. I feel fortunate.”

Why reforms alone won’t prevent a repeat of Tai Po fire
Systemic failures and human lapses both led to the preventable tragedy. More robust safeguards aside, individuals whose mistakes cost lives must also face consequences
3-MIN READ3-MIN
4
 Listen
Alice Wu is a political consultant and a former associate director of the Asia Pacific Media Network at UCLA. 
In the end, it was Winnie Ho Wing-yin, housing secretary at the time of the Wang Fuk Court fire in Tai Po, who took the rap. Her resignation came after weeks of talk within political circles suggesting that bureau chiefs would not have to bear responsibility for the tragedy that killed 168 people and displaced 1,984 families.
These suggestions were met with shock. Some spoke out against such talk, including Andrew Fung Wai-kwong, former information coordinator for the Chief Executive’s Office, and retired administrative officer Mike Rowse. Both reminded the public that Hong Kong has a ministerial system, and that political responsibility is very much part of the package.
The political accountability system created by the late Tung Chee-hwa demands that political appointees step down for failures on their watch, even if they were not personally responsible. Yet, for weeks, political accountability was hardly mentioned even though it was clear the report on the fire would implicate the Housing Bureau’s Independent Checking Unit, the Development Bureau’s Buildings Department, the Security Bureau’s Fire Services Department and the Labour and Welfare Bureau’s Labour Department.

Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-11-02
01:24:26 UTC
10:24:26 KST

Members of Nahariya's Christian community of South Lebanon Army (SLA) veterans were shocked on Sunday after worshippers discovered smashed statues and vandalized religious images inside a prayer hall used as a church by the community.
According to Father Yosef Yaakov, spokesperson for the Maronite community in Israel, a note written in English was left on the altar asking for forgiveness. Nahariya police opened an investigation into the incident, emphasizing that all possible leads were being examined.
The prayer hall is on municipal property adjacent to a municipal garden and serves the Lebanese Maronite community for prayer and religious ceremonies.
The community numbers approximately 1,100 people. Several dozen worshippers attend Sunday services, while hundreds gather for religious holidays.
'I don't know what got into me': Apology left on altar
Yaakov said the vandalism was discovered at approximately 5:30 p.m., when a worshipper entered the hall ahead of a prayer service scheduled for 7 p.m.
According to Yaakov, whoever damaged the statues and religious images left a note on the altar apologizing for the act and including a statement along the lines of "I don't know what came over me."
Yaakov stressed that the identities of those responsible and their motives remained unknown.
"We are waiting for the police to investigate," he said, adding that it was too early to determine whether the vandalism was motivated by religious hatred.
As the community awaits the results of the investigation, Yaakov described the pain felt by worshippers over the damage to a place of profound personal and religious significance.
He said the incident had caused anger and distress, as well as a feeling among community members that they were unwelcome.
Yaakov noted that families with children also attend services at the hall and that the vandalism had raised concerns about their safety, undermining the sense of security in a place where worshippers seek peace and spiritual comfort.
Maronite Church condemns vandalism: 'We will not respond to destruction with hatred'
The Maronite Archdiocese in Haifa issued a statement strongly condemning the incident.
The archdiocese described the vandalism as an attack on the sanctity of a place of worship and on the right of believers to practice their religion freely, safely, and with dignity.
Church leaders called on the authorities to investigate the incident, identify those responsible, and bring them to justice. They also demanded measures to protect the prayer hall and prevent similar incidents from recurring.
The archdiocese emphasized that the community would continue holding religious services at the site despite the damage.
"We will not allow this act of vandalism to deter us from exercising our natural right to pray and worship God. We will continue to use this hall and hold our prayers there, with faith, determination, and peace," the statement said.
The archdiocese further declared that "we do not respond to harm with harm, and we do not respond to destruction with hatred."
However, church leaders stressed that tolerance did not mean remaining silent in the face of harm or relinquishing their rights.
Police: 'All avenues of investigation are being examined'
Israel Police said the Nahariya police station had immediately opened an investigation after receiving a complaint about the vandalism.
Investigators were carrying out a range of investigative activities, and all possible avenues of inquiry were being examined, police said.
"The Israel Police views seriously any violation of holy places and freedom of worship, and will act decisively, exhausting all means at its disposal to locate those responsible for the act and bring them to justice," police emphasized.

In China, a significant increase in explored reserves of strategic minerals was recorded following a large-scale reassessment of deposits. Details

China found a new source of strategic zirconium

The discovery could increase domestic zirconium supplies and reduce China's dependence on imports.
Zirconium is used in the nuclear energy and aerospace industries. Rhenium is also of strategic importance, as it is used in heat-resistant alloys for jet engines.
